title: Google's three Imagen 4 API models shut down today, migration required
subtitle: August 17 is the deprecation date for imagen-4.0-generate-001 and its ultra and fast siblings, with Google directing developers to gemini-3.1-flash-image — and the API shape is not a drop-in swap.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: Google removed three Imagen 4 model IDs from the Gemini API today: imagen-4.0-generate-001, imagen-4.0-ultra-generate-001, and imagen-4.0-fast-generate-001. The shutdown date, August 17, 2026, has been on Google's deprecation table for months, and the company's recommended replacement is gemini-3.1-flash-image — the image-generation model in the Gemini 3.1 family, internally marketed as 'Nano Banana.'

The retired IDs handled the majority of production image-generation traffic on the Gemini API, so any application that still targeted them by name broke at the deprecation boundary today. The migration is not a name swap. The request and response schemas for gemini-3.1-flash-image differ from Imagen 4 — prompt structure, parameter names, and how negative prompts and reference images are attached all changed. Code that assumed a straight text-in, image-out interface needs an update.

Google has been consolidating its generative-media stack under the Gemini family for most of 2026, folding the separate Imagen and Veo API surfaces into Gemini's multimodal endpoints. Today's shutdown removes the last widely-used Imagen 4 GA IDs, leaving Vertex AI's enterprise tier as the only place a stable Imagen surface still exists for a small set of paying customers. The direction of travel is unified: one Gemini-shaped API for text, image, and video.

A takeaway for learners: every API you build on has a shutdown date, usually announced months before it lands. Read your provider's deprecation table quarterly and pin your code to model IDs you can explain, not model IDs you copied from a tutorial. A production app that breaks the day a well-flagged deprecation lands is a maintenance failure, not a vendor failure.
